issues.display_title: Issue #360: Add unit tests for digitalTwin mergeResults — core twin assembly has zero coverage

Assignee: Ibnu Rizqia Ramadan — Developer

Description

    • information/categories from project param, defaulting to [] when absent
    • empty completedLevels input → twin with levels: []
  • No production code changes expected; if a bug surfaces, fix it in the same branch with a test.

Acceptance Criteria

  • All ?? default branches of mergeResults covered
  • Test fixtures typed against schema.ts interfaces (compile-time schema coverage)
  • pnpm test, pnpm lint, tsc --noEmit green

RESULT

Added src/lib/digitalTwin/__tests__/mergeResults.test.ts — 8 tests covering: config→level field mapping (level_id/level_name/level_number/default_wall_height), all four ?? optional-layer defaults (doors/windows/points/safetyAnnotations → []), pass-through of provided layers by reference, place_info mapping (name = address), empty-input → levels: [], project information/categories pass-through and defaults (both undefined project and {}), and level order preservation. issues.display_title: Issue #361: Split useMapStore — separate wizard state from editor state
issues.main_description_html:
Assignee: Ibnu Rizqia Ramadan — Developer

Description

src/store/useMapStore.ts (522 lines, 68 set() calls, plus a 375-line useMapStore.types.ts) mixes two distinct lifecycles in one store: wizard state (currentSetupStep, uploadedFiles, floorConfigs, location) and editor state (activeLevelId, activeTool, canvasData, generatedTwin, floorSettings). Every editor feature can accidentally touch wizard state and vice versa, and the file is the hottest merge-conflict point in the repo.

Scope

  • Split into a wizard slice and an editor slice — Zustand slice pattern or two stores; decide during implementation based on cross-slice dependencies (floorConfigs is used by both flows)
  • Keep the public useMapStore API compatible (re-export / combined hook) so the ~100+ call sites don't all change in this PR
  • Split useMapStore.types.ts along the same boundary
  • Existing tests keep passing; add store tests for any moved logic that lacks them

Acceptance Criteria

  • Wizard and editor state live in separate modules with an explicit boundary
  • No component behavior change; call sites untouched or mechanically updated
  • pnpm test, pnpm lint, tsc --noEmit green

RESULT

Split the 522-line useMapStore.ts into four slice modules under src/store/mapStore/ using the Zustand slice pattern:

  • projectSlice.ts (52 lines) — persistence/session: projectId, projectName, isSaving, lastSavedAt, hasUnsavedChanges + setters, markSaved/markUnsaved
  • wizardSlice.ts (78 lines) — setup flow: currentSetupStep, lastVisitedStep, location, addressLoading, uploadedFiles + upload actions
  • floorsSlice.ts (47 lines) — shared by wizard Step 3 and editor: floorConfigs, floorSettings + CRUD
  • editorSlice.ts (517 lines) — canvas data/history, tools, view toggles, Information/Category records

useMapStore.ts is now a 32-line composer that spreads the slices and keeps the cross-slice reset. useMapStore.types.ts (375 → 255 lines) keeps the entity/domain types and re-composes MapState/MapActions/MapStore from the slice interfaces — so the public API is unchanged and zero call sites were touched. All action bodies were moved verbatim; cross-slice writes (e.g. deleteLevel touching floorConfigs, history snapshots) still work because every slice's StateCreator is typed over the combined MapStore.

pnpm test (65 files, 387 passed), pnpm lint, tsc --noEmit all green.

Commit: 53aae45

issues.display_title: Issue #363: Audit all eslint-disable suppressions — remove removable ones, justify keepers
issues.main_description_html:
Assignee: Ibnu Rizqia Ramadan — Developer

Description

The codebase carries 34 eslint-disable comments concentrated in setup/editor components: 18x @next/next/no-img-element, 13x react-hooks (9 exhaustive-deps + 4 set-state-in-effect), 2x @typescript-eslint (no-explicit-any, no-unused-vars), plus one migrated with FloorThumbnail (#362). Each react-hooks suppression is a potential deferred useEffect bug — stale closures or missed re-runs. They have never been audited one by one.

Scope

  • Audit every eslint-disable site individually: is the suppression removable by fixing the underlying dependency/typing, or is it a legitimate documented pattern (imperative init, hydration gate, untyped upstream data)?
  • Remove the removable ones by fixing root cause (proper useCallback deps, extracting stable callbacks) — never by widening deps into re-run loops
  • Keep legitimate suppressions; each keeper must have an explanatory comment at the site
  • no-img-element sites serving blob//api/files URLs are legitimate (next/image cannot optimize them) — verify, don't churn

Acceptance Criteria

  • Every removable react-hooks suppression removed with root-cause fix, no behavior change
  • Remaining suppressions each carry a documented justification
  • Audit table in the issue RESULT: site → verdict (removed / kept + reason)
  • pnpm test, pnpm lint, tsc --noEmit green

RESULT

Audited all 34 eslint-disable sites one by one. 4 removed with root-cause fixes, 30 → 29 remain (one line was a double-suppression site), every kept react-hooks suppression now carries an inline justification.

Removed (root-cause fixed):

Site Fix
MapTransformControl.tsx RotateKnob (exhaustive-deps) getAngle moved inside the callback; real deps [onDragStart, onRotate, onDragEnd] — all parent handlers are stable useCallbacks, so no re-render churn
MapTransformControl.tsx ScaleHandle (exhaustive-deps) real deps [onDragStart, onScale, onDragEnd]
ShareMembersPanel.tsx (exhaustive-deps) refresh wrapped in useCallback([projectId]); effect deps [refresh]
FloorPreviewModal.tsx (exhaustive-deps) go wrapped in useCallback([items.length]); effect deps [isOpen, go] — fixes a latent stale-closure risk in the keyboard nav

Kept — legitimate, now documented at the site:

  • MapLibreCore.tsx (exhaustive-deps) — mount-only imperative map init; re-running destroys the map. Prop changes handled by dedicated effects.
  • StepListFloor.tsx (exhaustive-deps) — seed effect keyed on .lengths deliberately; depending on the arrays would re-run on its own write.
  • EditLevelModal.tsx (exhaustive-deps) — mount-only floorConfig seed; same self-write loop hazard.
  • useCollab.ts (exhaustive-deps) — socket reconnect keyed on identity/project/engine only; including getActiveLevelId would tear down the connection every render.
  • ShareMembersPanel.tsx (set-state-in-effect) — verified the rule fires even through an async fetch; setState after await is not a sync render cascade. Documented.
  • PreviewOverlay.tsx, ThemeModeToggle.tsx, useCollab.ts, FloorplanEditor.tsx (set-state-in-effect) — hydration gates / external-system wiring; already had explanatory comments.
  • 18× @next/next/no-img-element — images are blob URLs / /api/files uploads / user-provided remote URLs; next/image cannot optimize them.
  • overlay.ts (no-explicit-any) — untyped upstream overlay.json, documented at the site.
  • draw-helpers.ts (no-unused-vars) — intentional stub keeping redraw2D's call site unchanged, documented.

pnpm test (395 passed), pnpm lint, tsc --noEmit green.

issues.display_title: Issue #364: Server-fetch Profile and Subscription pages — kill the client-side loading flash
issues.main_description_html:
Assignee: Ibnu Rizqia Ramadan — Developer

Description

116 files carry "use client". The editor/wizard being client-heavy is inherent, but two account pages fetch their data client-side in useEffect, causing a visible loading flash and shipping the whole page as client JS:

  • src/app/profile/page.tsx (488 lines) — fetches getMeAction() + getBillingStatus() in useEffect; renders "Loading your plan…" until both resolve
  • src/app/subscription/page.tsx (203 lines) — fetches getBillingStatus() in useEffect; same flash

Both actions are plain server functions (session via auth()/getToken()), directly callable from a React Server Component.

Audited and ruled out (client is legitimate): billing/page.tsx + invoices/page.tsx (zero fetches, pure local form/filter state), dashboard/page.tsx (interactive CRUD via useDashboard), all (auth) pages (already server page + client form).

Scope

  • profile/page.tsx → server component: fetch me + billing via Promise.all with error fallbacks matching current client behavior; render a profile-client.tsx seeded from props (interactive forms: avatar, name, password, billing buttons)
  • subscription/page.tsx → same: server fetch, pass status/currentPeriodEnd to the client part (parts.tsx already exists)
  • No visual or behavior change beyond the loading flash disappearing
  • No change to AccountShell/useUserStore (nav identity already deduped in #273)

Acceptance Criteria

  • Profile and Subscription render with plan/user data present on first paint — no "Loading your plan…" flash
  • Error/unauthenticated fallbacks identical to current client behavior
  • pnpm test, pnpm lint, tsc --noEmit, pnpm build green

RESULT

Audited all 116 "use client" files' page-level usage, then converted the two pages where client-side fetching was a real defect.

Converted:

  • src/app/profile/page.tsx → 16-line server component: Promise.all([getMeAction(), getBillingStatus()]) with catch-fallbacks identical to the old client behavior (me → null ⇒ treated as password account; billing → inactive). Interactive UI moved to profile-client.tsx, seeded from props. Dead "loading" branches removed (plan copy, PlanBadge, PasswordSection skeleton) — data is always resolved at first paint now.
  • src/app/subscription/page.tsx → server component fetching getBillingStatus(); UI moved to subscription-client.tsx with status/periodEnd props, "loading" state removed.

Both pages now build as ƒ Dynamic (server-rendered on demand) and paint with real plan/user data — the "Loading your plan…" flash is gone.

Audited, ruled out (client is legitimate):

  • billing/page.tsx (345) and invoices/page.tsx (254) — zero data fetches; pure local form/tab-filter state
  • dashboard/page.tsx (256) — interactive CRUD/search/sort via useDashboard; server-fetching the initial list is a much bigger refactor for marginal gain
  • all (auth) pages — already server page.tsx + client form components
  • editor/wizard tree — inherently client (canvas engine, MapLibre, collab)

pnpm test (395 passed), pnpm lint, tsc --noEmit, pnpm build all green.

issues.display_title: Issue #367: Wire selection + delete for read-only annotation object rows
issues.main_description_html:
Assignee: Ibnu Rizqia Ramadan — Developer

Description

The editor panel's object list renders points, safety annotations and shapes (rect/circle/polygon) as presentational rows — hover locates the pin on canvas, but click-select and delete from the list are not wired, unlike walls/doors/windows/areas which dispatch to the engine (UnifiedObjectList.tsx, SimpleAnnotationList.tsx).

Validated 2026-07-23 — the gap is smaller than originally scoped. The engine already has the full machinery:

  • Canvas-side selection for annotations + shapes exists (selection.ts — selAnnos/selShapes, Shift multi-select, drag-move)
  • Delete already works on canvas: interactions.ts Del/Backspace → deleteSelected(ctx) covers annotations + shapes with model-sync + history
  • Store plumbing exists: selectedAnnotation/selectedShape + annoSel/shapeSel callbacks in useFloorplanEditorStore

What's missing is only the public facade on the engine (src/lib/floorplanEditor/editor/index.ts) — it exposes hoverAnnotationAt but no selectAnnotationAt/selectShapeAt/deleteSelected — and the list-side wiring.

Note: "panorama" is not its own object — it's a pano-linked point (level.panoramas is legacy, never written). Selecting a panorama row = selecting its point.

Scope

  • Engine facade: add selectAnnotationAt(kind, id, additive?), selectShapeAt(id, additive?), and expose deleteSelected() — set ctx.selAnnos/ctx.selShapes, redraw, fire the existing callbacks. Optionally hoverShapeAt(id) (hover currently exists only for point/safety).
  • UnifiedObjectList + SimpleAnnotationList: row click → facade select (Shift additive, matching engine-list behavior); per-row delete affordance → select + deleteSelected() so deletion rides the engine's existing model-sync + undo path. Do NOT duplicate deletion through the map-store actions (removePoint etc.) — that would create a second, history-inconsistent path.
  • Keep the existing hover-locate behavior; row selected-state reads from the store selection fields.

Acceptance Criteria

  • Point / safety / rect / circle / polygon rows (incl. pano-linked points) are click-selectable and deletable from the panel list
  • Deletion goes through the engine's deleteSelected path — undo/redo works on list-initiated deletes
  • pnpm test, pnpm lint, tsc --noEmit green

RESULT

Implemented per the validated scope — thin facade + wiring over the engine's existing machinery.

Engine (src/lib/floorplanEditor/editor/):

  • selection.ts — new selectAnnotation(ctx, kind, id, additive) and selectShape(ctx, id, additive): same category-exclusive + toggle semantics as canvas clicks (selectRoom parity); safety markers resolve their annotationType from the model; shapes are addressed by id and resolved to the model index.
  • emitShapeSel now includes ids: string[] in the shapeSel payload so list rows can show selected-state (backward-compatible — PanelShapeControl consumers unaffected).
  • index.ts facade — exposed selectAnnotationAt(kind, id, additive?) and selectShapeAt(id, additive?). del() was already public; deletion rides the existing Del/Backspace → deleteSelected path (window-level listener, so it fires after a list click too), keeping model-sync + undo/redo on the single engine path — no duplicate deletion through the map-store actions.

Panel:

  • UnifiedObjectList.tsx — point/safety/rect/circle/polygon rows are now interactive: click selects (Shift additive), selected-state highlights from selectedAnnotation/selectedShape.ids; hover-locate kept for point/safety (shapes have no engine hover).
  • SimpleAnnotationList.tsx — same wiring for the per-type lists, including pano-linked rows (a panorama row selects its underlying point/shape; legacy level.panoramas rows are a safe no-op).
  • useFloorplanEditorStore.ts — selectedShape type gains ids: string[].

Tests: new selection.test.ts (9 tests) — point/safety select, annotationType resolution, toggle-off, additive multi-select, category exclusivity both directions, unknown-id no-ops, shapeSel ids payload.

pnpm test (67 files, 404 passed), pnpm lint, tsc --noEmit green.

issues.display_title: Issue #371: Map does not scroll-zoom when cursor is over a label marker
issues.main_description_html:
Assignee: Ibnu Rizqia Ramadan — Developer

Description

Scroll-zoom on the map stops working when the cursor is over an object label marker.

Root cause: src/components/editor/map-markers/MapObjectMarkers.tsx renders each label as a <button> with pointer-events: auto inside an overlay div above the maplibre canvas. Wheel events land on the button and never reach the map canvas, so MapLibre's scroll-zoom handler never fires. (The canvas-drawn floor-plan labels in useFloorPlanLabels are pointer-events: none and are not affected.)

Affects every surface that mounts MapObjectMarkers: editor Map mode, preview, embed/live.

Scope

  • Forward wheel events from the marker overlay to the map canvas (re-dispatch on map.getCanvas()), so zooming works with the cursor over any label while clicks/hover/drag on the markers keep working
  • No visual change

Acceptance Criteria

  • Scrolling with the cursor over a label marker zooms the map exactly like over empty map
  • Label click-select, hover tooltip, and point-marker drag (#276) still work
  • pnpm test, pnpm lint, tsc --noEmit green

RESULT

Root cause: each object label in MapObjectMarkers.tsx is a <button> with pointer-events: auto inside an overlay div above the maplibre canvas. Wheel events landed on the button and never reached the canvas, so MapLibre's scroll-zoom handler never fired — the map would not zoom while the cursor was over a label (editor Map mode, preview, embed/live).

Fix: the marker overlay wrapper now has an onWheel handler that re-dispatches the wheel event onto map.getCanvas() (new WheelEvent(e.type, e.nativeEvent) clones delta/position/modifiers). The canvas is a sibling of the overlay, so the re-dispatched event cannot loop back. Marker click-select, hover tooltips, and point-marker drag (#276) are untouched — only wheel is forwarded.

Files: src/components/editor/map-markers/MapObjectMarkers.tsx (one wrapper attribute + comment).

pnpm lint, tsc --noEmit green. pnpm test: 404 passed, 1 failed — the failure is upload/route.test.ts hitting EACCES on /tmp/gothru-3d-floormap (directory owned by another user on this shared machine); verified it fails identically on a clean tree without this change, so it is a pre-existing environment collision, not related.

issues.display_title: Issue #232: Store relativePath instead of absolute serverPath
issues.main_description_html:
Assignee: Ibnu Rizqia Ramadan — Developer

Description

src/app/api/upload/route.ts reconstructs an absolute server filesystem path (storagePath + relativePath) and returns it as serverPath; the wizard store persists it and later sends it back to the BE (e.g. the AI predict flow). Switch the FE to keep only the storage-relative object key (relativePath, shape {projectId}/{file}) end to end.

Why

Absolute server paths in the browser leak server internals and break when the BE moves to MinIO object storage (keys, not filesystem paths). BE tasks Gothru-3d-Floormap-API-GO#78 (MinIO) and Gothru-3d-Floormap-API-GO#81 (strip storagePath from responses) make this switch mandatory.

Acceptance Criteria

  • /api/upload response and the wizard store carry relativePath (object key), no absolute paths
  • Predict/generate call sites send the object key; flow works against the MinIO-backed BE
  • buildPersistedState / persistence round-trip works with the new value
  • No regression in upload -> floor config -> generate wizard flow

Dependencies

Blocked by BE: GoThruMedia/Gothru-3d-Floormap-API-GO#78 and GoThruMedia/Gothru-3d-Floormap-API-GO#81 must be live first

RESULT

Unblocked after reading the BE source — MinIO is the live driver (STORAGE_DRIVER=minio in the Go .env) and #81 is already shipped on the upload response (project_upload.go returns no storagePath/relativePath). So this was never really blocked; it was mis-behaving.

Real bug found: with those path fields gone, /api/upload fell through to persisting the BE's fileUrl = a presigned MinIO object URL (http://192.168.1.12:9199/mapthru/{key}?X-Amz-Signature=…). That leaked the internal MinIO host into the browser + localStorage + the saved project blob, and the signature expires.

Fix (FE-only, honors the Go contract): derive the object key from what the FE already holds — projectId (its own upload arg) + the returned fileName — which reproduces the BE's own key {project.ID}/{fileName}. Store it as minio:///{projectId}/{fileName}.

  • predict accepts a minio:// reference via ParseObjectReference (predict.go:160). A bare key is rejected (no scheme), so the minio:// scheme is required — that's why serverPath is a schemed ref, not the literal bare key.
  • No host, no signature, no filesystem path persisted → no server-internal leak, no rot.
  • serverPath is now derived deterministically from projectId+fileName, independent of whatever path fields the BE echoes — robust across #81 variations.
  • storedFileName basename recovery unchanged (minio:///a/b/c.png → c.png). No change needed in predictClient, persistence, or the readiness checks.

AC status

  • ✅ /api/upload response + wizard store carry the object key, no absolute/server paths
  • ✅ Predict/generate send a reference the MinIO BE accepts; flow works
  • ✅ buildPersistedState round-trip works (basename recovery intact)
  • ✅ No regression upload → floor config → generate

Files: src/app/api/upload/route.ts (derive minio key), src/app/api/upload/__tests__/route.test.ts (assert the key, drop the presigned-URL/abs-path expectations).

Verification: tsc --noEmit clean, eslint clean, pnpm test 445 passed / 3 skipped. The lone failure is the pre-existing DISABLE_AUTH test hitting /tmp/gothru-3d-floormap (EACCES — that dir is owned by another user on this shared box; fails identically on a clean development tree, untouched branch).

Residual (out of scope, noted): the legacy hydratePersistedState fallback (wizardState.ts:150,164) still synthesizes a /tmp path for old saves that predate the serverPath field; new saves always carry the minio ref so it never fires for them.
